name: sol_integrations_uniswap_1
description: On-chain slippage/minimum-output calculation manipulable via price oracle or reserve manipulation
question: The source file in `source` computes a swap or liquidity operation's minimum acceptable output (slippage tolerance) internally on-chain, by deriving an expected price or amount from current pool reserves, spot price, or a live on-chain oracle at execution time, rather than accepting a caller-supplied minimum-output/maximum-input amount calculated off-chain, so an attacker can manipulate the on-chain price/reserves (e.g., via a flash loan or sandwich trade) to widen the effective slippage and extract value; this does not apply if the function already requires an externally supplied minAmountOut/maxAmountIn parameter that is enforced without being overridden by an on-chain-derived value.
criteria: swap() computes minOut = getReserves()-derived expected price * (1-slippageBps) inside the contract instead of accepting a user-supplied minOut
addLiquidity() derives minimum token amounts from the pool's current spot price fetched on-chain right before the trade executes
function ignores any passed-in minAmountOut parameter and instead recalculates the acceptable amount from a live on-chain oracle call
router wrapper computes acceptable slippage bounds using Uniswap pair's current reserves at call time and enforces those instead of caller-specified bounds
